title: The Mtr4 Arch Domain is Required for RNA Movement Between Active Sites in the Saccharomyces cerevisiae TRAMP Complex
content: The TRAMP (Trf4-Air2-Mtr4 Polyadenylation) complex plays an essential role in RNA surveillance pathways by targeting and delivering RNA substrates for degradation by the nuclear exosome. In S. cerevisiae, the TRAMP complex consists of a non-canonical poly(A) polymerase (Trf4), a zinc knuckle RNA binding protein (Air2), and a 3’-5’ RNA helicase (Mtr4). Complex formation results in modulation of Trf4 polymerase activity and enhancement of Mtr4 helicase activity. The interplay between TRAMP components is critical to understanding how TRAMP engages and processes RNA substrates.
